title: Review shared artifact, cache, IO, bundle, and serialization module families
scope: Primary ownership for src/shared artifact, cache, IO, bundle, and serialization helpers assigned to #411 in the shared-module ledger.

summary.overallAssessment: This shared surface is broadly useful and already owns many of the repo's right low-level seams, but it must stay deliberately layered. Recent work made manifest.js and bundle-io.js facade-oriented, moved manifest entry selection and columnar rows into narrow artifact owners, split bundle behavior, separated generic binary-columnar frame reading from the async chunk_meta adapter, and kept sync token_postings binary decode local to preserve the sync API. The remaining cleanup opportunities are the larger loader cores, the deleted files facade handoff, atomic persistence, cache layering documentation, and generic JSON-stream boundaries; compression pooling and byte accounting now have their own JSON-stream owners, binary-columnar JSON row decode has its own loader leaf, and core streaming row dispatch has its own loader leaf.

clusterFindings.assessment: This family is valuable and correctly shared. Manifest entry selection, manifest source resolution, core streaming row dispatch, columnar row inflation, generic binary-columnar frame reading, binary-columnar JSON row decode, and the async chunk_meta binary-columnar adapter now have separate owners. Sync token_postings binary-columnar decode stays in token-postings.js to preserve its public sync API. The remaining high-value work is keeping manifest.js facade-oriented without weakening source resolution, fallback, or budget behavior.

The bundle behavior split is complete: bundle-io.js is now a re-export-only facade, path/name/format helpers live in bundle-io-paths.js, checksum constants live in bundle-io-constants.js, and read/write/patch/support behavior has narrow owner modules. The former atomic-persistence.js facade has been removed; temp-path, replace-file, replace-dir, and persistence-helpers now own the low-level persistence mechanics directly.

The root cache facade has been removed. Cache layer descriptions, byte estimation, LRU/reporting, CAS path/hash, metadata, object write/touch, enumeration, lease reads, cache-root, cache-key, JSON-file, and policy behavior now have explicit narrow owners.

The former root files.js and json-stream.js facades have been removed. Path predicates and conversion now live in file-paths.js, file-range/existence/safe JSON reads live in file-read.js, object/array JSON writers live in json-stream/json-writers.js, and JSONL batch writing, compression pooling, byte accounting, sharded writing, stream, compression, offset, and atomic helpers remain in their narrow json-stream family owners.

The contract and metadata helpers that did not belong in this bucket have now moved out. The remaining specialized concern here is provenance metadata, which is coherent but should stay clearly bounded so additional contract or metadata surfaces do not drift back into the generic storage family.

highestPriorityFollowUps.reason: The manifest facade now delegates entry selection and source resolution to narrower artifact owners; keep it facade-oriented and prevent new implementation drift.
The behavior split is complete; keep this file re-export-only and preserve the narrow bundle-io/read, write, patch, and support ownership.
The root cache facade has been removed; keep cache layer descriptions, byte estimation, LRU, and reporting behavior in narrow cache owners.
